units.translation: And they, terrified in their minds, will come.
And the captured women are to be led away.
And some things he even carries fire for.
We are on the side of the rulers, and they on the side of the defeated.
And he, having a savage spirit, stands in the way.
And they ended in this way.
And how Xerxes sees him.
And he, doing nothing else but cowering, offered his body.
And he, as soon as he heard.
And they, not without order, were preparing their meal.
And they struck them like tunny-fish.
And they, throughout the land of Asia, are no longer ruled by Persians.
And him Artaphrenes killed by treachery.
They suffer no less, and some things they are about to suffer.
And to them speak a lament of the same tongue, ailinon, ailinon.
And he, doing nothing else but cowering, offered his body.
And they shone in response.
And he is not pious.
And they hold tombs there around the wall.
And some things were on land and were present.
And they, struck by horn, went off by force.
And he, without the lyre, nevertheless sings a dirge of the Fury.
And they, who never expected it, reaped well.
And she, speaking ill-omened words, calls upon the god.
And they do not sleep.
And them pure night holds.
And they are wanton beyond measure.
And she is hated with full justice.
And the orphaned ones are pressed by fasting hunger.
And these things are not at all charmed.
And she cried out from sleep.
And she lamented over this suffering with fear.
And these things are well.
And in time I say that all Argives bear witness to these things.
And he, having escaped, is gone.
And he, having strength, wishes.
And this is not present.
And she, as a stranger to a stranger, saved the shoot.
And she is born.
And I am the cause of these things.
And he himself, singing, is himself the killer.
With the mattock of Zeus, by which the ground has been worked.
With a double whip, which Ares loves.
The fire-kindling forethought which the wretched child-destroying Thestias devised.
Of mortals, to whom vain self-deeds befall.
The city, which even Zeus rules.
Having dishonored the son of the cow, whom he himself once begot as offspring.

Of man-destroying beasts, which indeed the earth sent up, where it should be noted that τὰ δή [these indeed] is placed at the beginning of the trimeter without metrical necessity for ἃ δή [which indeed], unless this very thing is to be restored. See the Oxford note on Sophocles OC 35.
Argos, whom Hermes, the son of Earth, killed.
With prayers ask for the things which desire holds for you to obtain.
The life-giving race, which indeed is truly of Zeus, where Porson rightly reads γένος τόδε [this race].
To hasten something of what the mind's counsel brings.
The public thing, which strengthens the city.
Butler restored τὸν [the] for ὃν [whom].
A cup, in which he slanders.
Where the Phorcides dwell, the ancient maidens, unless with Hermann one should write Φορκυνίδες [daughters of Phorcys].
Those who worship Adrasteia are wise.
Where do they say Athens is established on the earth?
Alas, how I groan when I remember Athens.
Of Seisamas, that is, of the son of Megabatas.
The wheat-rich land of Aphrodite, where Hermann rightly reads τὰν Ἀφροδίτας [the land of Aphrodite].
And may the Lycian be gracious to all the youth.
Of Themis of straight counsel.
